problems.problem_statement: Let `f(x)` be a function defined as: `f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{x^2 - 9}{x - 3} & \text{if } x < 3 \\ kx - 4 & \text{if } x \geq 3 \end{cases}`. For what value of the constant `k` is the function `f(x)` continuous at `x=3`?
problems.solution: For `f(x)` to be continuous at `x=3`, we must have `\lim_{x \to 3^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 3^+} f(x) = f(3)`. First, we compute the left-hand limit: `\lim_{x \to 3^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 3^-} \frac{x^2 - 9}{x - 3} = \lim_{x \to 3^-} \frac{(x-3)(x+3)}{x-3} = \lim_{x \to 3^-} (x+3) = 3+3 = 6`. Next, we compute the right-hand limit and the function value at `x=3`: `\lim_{x \to 3^+} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 3^+} (kx - 4) = 3k - 4`. Also, `f(3) = k(3) - 4 = 3k - 4`. For continuity, we set the left-hand limit equal to the right-hand limit: `6 = 3k - 4`. Solving for `k` gives `10 = 3k`, so `k = \frac{10}{3}`.

scaffolding.hint: Recall the definition of continuity at a point `c`. A function `f(x)` is continuous at `x=c` if `\lim_{x \to c} f(x) = f(c)`. This implies that the left-hand limit, the right-hand limit, and the function value must all be equal: `\lim_{x \to c^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to c^+} f(x) = f(c)`.
Calculate the left-hand limit as `x` approaches 3: `\lim_{x \to 3^-} \frac{x^2 - 9}{x - 3}`. You will need to factor the numerator to resolve the indeterminate form `\frac{0}{0}`.
Calculate the right-hand limit as `x` approaches 3: `\lim_{x \to 3^+} (kx - 4)`. This can be found by direct substitution and will be an expression involving `k`.
Equate the results from the left-hand limit and the right-hand limit to ensure the overall limit exists. Solve the resulting linear equation for the constant `k`.
